title.en: House of King Goujian of Yue
title.raw: 《越王句踐世家》 House of King Goujian of Yue

sentences.zh: 越王句踐，其先禹之苗裔，而夏后帝少康之庶子也。

translations.literal: King Goujian of Yue was descended from Yu and from a younger son of Emperor Shaokang of the Xia royal house.
translations.idiomatic: King Goujian of Yue was descended from Yu and from a younger son of Emperor Shaokang of the Xia royal house.

sentences.zh: 封於會稽，以奉守禹之祀。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed at Kuaiji to maintain the sacrifices to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed at Kuaiji to maintain the sacrifices to Yu.

sentences.zh: 文身斷發，披草萊而邑焉。

translations.literal: His people tattooed their bodies, cut their hair short, cleared the grassy wilderness, and founded settlements there.
translations.idiomatic: His people tattooed their bodies, cut their hair short, cleared the grassy wilderness, and founded settlements there.

sentences.zh: 後二十餘世，至於允常。

translations.literal: After more than twenty generations, it reached Yun Chang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty generations, it reached Yun Chang.

sentences.zh: 允常之時，與吳王闔廬戰而相怨伐。

translations.literal: In Yunchang’s time, he fought King Helü of Wu, and the two states attacked one another in mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunchang’s time, he fought King Helü of Wu, and the two states attacked one another in mutual resentment.

sentences.zh: 允常卒，子句踐立，是為越王。

translations.literal: Yunchang died, and his son Goujian came to the throne as king of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang died, and his son Goujian came to the throne as king of Yue.

sentences.zh: 元年，吳王闔廬聞允常死，乃興師伐越。

translations.literal: In the first year, Wu wang He Lu heard that Yun Chang had died and then raised troops to attack Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, King He Lu of Wu heard that Yun Chang had died and then raised troops to attack Yue.

sentences.zh: 越王句踐使死士挑戰，三行，至吳陳，呼而自剄。

translations.literal: King Goujian of Yue sent condemned warriors to challenge Wu to battle. In three ranks they reached the Wu lines, shouted, and cut their own throats.
translations.idiomatic: King Goujian of Yue sent condemned warriors to challenge Wu to battle. In three ranks they reached the Wu lines, shouted, and cut their own throats.

sentences.zh: 吳師觀之，越因襲擊吳師，吳師敗於檇李，射傷吳王闔廬。

translations.literal: The Wu army stared at them, and Yue took the opportunity to launch a surprise attack. Wu was defeated at Zuili, and King Helü of Wu was wounded by an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu army stared at them, and Yue took the opportunity to launch a surprise attack. Wu was defeated at Zuili, and King Helü of Wu was wounded by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 闔廬且死，告其子夫差曰：「必毋忘越。」

translations.literal: As Helü was about to die, he told his son Fuchai, “You must never forget Yue.”
translations.idiomatic: As Helü was about to die, he told his son Fuchai, “You must never forget Yue.”

sentences.zh: 三年，句踐聞吳王夫差日夜勒兵，且以報越，越欲先吳未發往伐之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Goujian heard that King Fuchai of Wu was drilling troops day and night, intending to avenge himself on Yue. Yue wanted to attack Wu first, before Wu set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Goujian heard that King Fuchai of Wu was drilling troops day and night, intending to avenge himself on Yue. Yue wanted to attack Wu first, before Wu set out.

sentences.zh: 范蠡諫曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Fan Li remonstrated: “This must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li remonstrated: “This must not be done.

sentences.zh: 臣聞兵者凶器也，戰者逆德也，爭者事之末也。

translations.literal: Your minister has heard that weapons are inauspicious instruments, that warfare is contrary to virtue, and that contention is the last resort of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that weapons are inauspicious instruments, that warfare is contrary to virtue, and that contention is the last resort of affairs.

sentences.zh: 陰謀逆德，好用凶器，試身於所末，上帝禁之，行者不利。」

translations.literal: To plot in secret against virtue, delight in using instruments of misfortune, and test oneself in what should be the last resort is forbidden by the Supreme Deity; those who act this way will not prosper.”
translations.idiomatic: To plot in secret against virtue, delight in using instruments of misfortune, and test oneself in what should be the last resort is forbidden by the Supreme Deity; those who act this way will not prosper.”

sentences.zh: 越王曰：「吾已決之矣。」

translations.literal: The king of Yue said, “I have already decided.”
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yue said, “I have already decided.”

sentences.zh: 遂興師。

translations.literal: They then raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: They then raised troops.

sentences.zh: 吳王聞之，悉發精兵擊越，敗之夫椒。

translations.literal: The king of Wu heard of this and sent all his elite troops to attack Yue, defeating them at Fujiao.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Wu heard of this and sent all his elite troops to attack Yue, defeating them at Fujiao.

sentences.zh: 越王乃以餘兵五千人保棲於會稽。

translations.literal: The Yue king then took his remaining five thousand troops and held fast at Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue king then took his remaining five thousand troops and held fast at Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 吳王追而圍之。

translations.literal: The Wu wang pursued and surrounded them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu king pursued and surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 越王謂范蠡曰：「以不聽子故至於此，為之柰何？」

translations.literal: The king of Yue said to Fan Li, “Because I did not listen to you, I have come to this point. What is to be done?”
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yue said to Fan Li, “Because I did not listen to you, I have come to this point. What is to be done?”

sentences.zh: 蠡對曰：「持滿者與天，定傾者與人，節事者以地。

translations.literal: Fan Li replied: “When something is full, one should align with Heaven; when something is overturned, one should align with people; when regulating affairs, one should accord with the land.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li replied: “When something is full, one should align with Heaven; when something is overturned, one should align with people; when regulating affairs, one should accord with the land.

sentences.zh: 卑辭厚禮以遺之，不許，而身與之市。」

translations.literal: Humble words thick gifts to send them, if not permitted, then body with them bargain.'
translations.idiomatic: Send them humble words and generous gifts. If they do not permit it, then you yourself must go and bargain with the Wu king in person.'

sentences.zh: 句踐曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Gou Jian said: 'Yes.'
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian said: 'Yes.'

sentences.zh: 乃令大夫種行成於吳，膝行頓首曰：「君王亡臣句踐使陪臣種敢告下執事：句踐請為臣，妻為妾。」

translations.literal: He then ordered Grandee Zhong to go and make peace with Wu. Zhong walked on his knees, knocked his head to the ground, and said: “Goujian, fugitive servant of Your Majesty, sends his attendant minister Zhong to address those below you: Goujian asks to become your minister, and his wife your concubine.”
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Grandee Zhong to go and make peace with Wu. Zhong walked on his knees, knocked his head to the ground, and said: “Goujian, fugitive servant of Your Majesty, sends his attendant minister Zhong to address those below you: Goujian asks to become your minister, and his wife your concubine.”

sentences.zh: 吳王將許之。

translations.literal: The Wu wang was about to permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu king was about to permit it.

sentences.zh: 子胥言於吳王曰：「天以越賜吳，勿許也。」

translations.literal: Zi Xu spoke to Wu wang said: 'Heaven with Yue grants Wu, do not permit.'
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xu spoke to the Wu king, saying: 'Heaven grants Yue to Wu. Do not permit it.'

sentences.zh: 種還，以報句踐。

translations.literal: Zhong returned to report to Gou Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong returned to report to Gou Jian.

sentences.zh: 句踐欲殺妻子，燔寶器，觸戰以死。

translations.literal: Gou Jian desired to kill his wife and children, burn the treasure vessels, and fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian desired to kill his wife and children, burn the treasure vessels, and fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 種止句踐曰：「夫吳太宰嚭貪，可誘以利，請閒行言之。」

translations.literal: Zhong stopped Goujian and said: “The Grand Administrator Pi of Wu is greedy and can be tempted with profit. Please let me go secretly and speak with him.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhong stopped Goujian and said: “The Grand Administrator Pi of Wu is greedy and can be tempted with profit. Please let me go secretly and speak with him.”

sentences.zh: 於是句踐以美女寶器令種閒獻吳太宰嚭。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gou Jian commanded Zhong to secretly offer beautiful women and treasure vessels to Wu's grand administrator Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gou Jian commanded Zhong to secretly offer beautiful women and treasure vessels to the Wu grand administrator Pi.

sentences.zh: 嚭受，乃見大夫種於吳王。

translations.literal: Pi accepted and then presented Grandee Zhong to the Wu wang.
translations.idiomatic: Pi accepted and then presented Grandee Zhong to the Wu king.

sentences.zh: 種頓首言曰：「願大王赦句踐之罪，盡入其寶器。

translations.literal: Zhong knocked his head to the ground and said: “I hope Your Majesty will pardon Goujian’s offense and accept all his precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong knocked his head to the ground and said: “I hope Your Majesty will pardon Goujian’s offense and accept all his precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 不幸不赦，句踐將盡殺其妻子，燔其寶器，悉五千人觸戰，必有當也。」

translations.literal: If you do not pardon him, Gou Jian will kill his wife and children to the last, burn his treasure vessels, and all five thousand men will fight to the death. There will certainly be stiff resistance.'
translations.idiomatic: If you do not pardon him, Gou Jian will kill his wife and children to the last, burn his treasure vessels, and all five thousand men will fight to the death. There will certainly be stiff resistance.'

sentences.zh: 嚭因說吳王曰：「越以服為臣，若將赦之，此國之利也。」

translations.literal: Pi then persuaded the king of Wu: “Yue has submitted as your minister. If you pardon it, this will profit the state.”
translations.idiomatic: Pi then persuaded the king of Wu: “Yue has submitted as your minister. If you pardon it, this will profit the state.”

sentences.zh: 吳王將許之。

translations.literal: The Wu wang was about to permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu king was about to permit it.

sentences.zh: 子胥進諫曰：「今不滅越，後必悔之。

translations.literal: Zi Xu advanced admonished said: 'Now not extinguish Yue, later certainly regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xu advanced and admonished, saying: 'If we do not extinguish the state of Yue now, we will certainly regret it later.

sentences.zh: 句踐賢君，種、蠡良臣，若反國，將為亂。」

translations.literal: Gou Jian worthy lord, Zhong, Li good ministers, if return country, will cause chaos.'
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian is a worthy lord, and Zhong and Li are good ministers. If they return to their country, they will cause chaos.'

sentences.zh: 吳王弗聽，卒赦越，罷兵而歸。

translations.literal: The Wu wang did not listen. He finally pardoned Yue, dismissed the troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu king did not listen. He finally pardoned Yue, dismissed the troops, and returned.

sentences.zh: 句踐之困會稽也，喟然嘆曰：「吾終於此乎？」

translations.literal: When Goujian was trapped at Kuaiji, he sighed deeply and said, “Will I end here?”
translations.idiomatic: When Goujian was trapped at Kuaiji, he sighed deeply and said, “Will I end here?”

sentences.zh: 種曰：「湯系夏臺，文王囚羑里，晉重耳奔翟，齊小白奔莒，其卒王霸。

translations.literal: Zhong said: “Tang was bound at Xiatai, King Wen was imprisoned at Youli, Chong’er of Jin fled to the Di, and Xiaobai of Qi fled to Ju, yet in the end they became kings and hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: “Tang was bound at Xiatai, King Wen was imprisoned at Youli, Chong’er of Jin fled to the Di, and Xiaobai of Qi fled to Ju, yet in the end they became kings and hegemons.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，何遽不為福乎？」

translations.literal: Seen from this, how do we know this will not quickly become a blessing?”
translations.idiomatic: Seen from this, how do we know this will not quickly become a blessing?”

sentences.zh: 吳既赦越，越王句踐反國，乃苦身焦思，置膽於坐，坐臥即仰膽，飲食亦嘗膽也。

translations.literal: After Wu pardoned Yue, King Goujian of Yue returned to his state. He then tormented his body and strained his thoughts, placing gall at his seat; whenever he sat or lay down he looked up at the gall, and when eating and drinking he tasted it.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu pardoned Yue, King Goujian of Yue returned to his state. He then tormented his body and strained his thoughts, placing gall at his seat; whenever he sat or lay down he looked up at the gall, and when eating and drinking he tasted it.

sentences.zh: 曰：「女忘會稽之恥邪？」

translations.literal: He would say, “Have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji?”
translations.idiomatic: He would say, “Have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji?”

sentences.zh: 身自耕作，夫人自織，食不加肉，衣不重采，折節下賢人，厚遇賓客，振貧弔死，與百姓同其勞。

translations.literal: He personally tilled the fields, and his wife personally wove. His food had no added meat, his clothing no layered colors. He lowered himself before worthy men, treated guests generously, aided the poor, mourned the dead, and shared the people’s labors.
translations.idiomatic: He personally tilled the fields, and his wife personally wove. His food had no added meat, his clothing no layered colors. He lowered himself before worthy men, treated guests generously, aided the poor, mourned the dead, and shared the people’s labors.

sentences.zh: 欲使范蠡治國政，蠡對曰：「兵甲之事，種不如蠡；

translations.literal: He wanted Fan Li to govern the affairs of the state. Fan Li replied: “In matters of armor and weapons, Zhong is not as good as I am;
translations.idiomatic: He wanted Fan Li to govern the affairs of the state. Fan Li replied: “In matters of armor and weapons, Zhong is not as good as I am;

sentences.zh: 填撫國家，親附百姓，蠡不如種。」

translations.literal: but in pacifying the state and drawing the people close, I am not as good as Zhong.”
translations.idiomatic: but in pacifying the state and drawing the people close, I am not as good as Zhong.”

sentences.zh: 於是舉國政屬大夫種，而使范蠡與大夫柘稽行成，為質於吳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entrusted the affairs of the state to Grandee Zhong, and sent Fan Li and Grandee Zheji to make peace and serve as hostages in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he entrusted the affairs of the state to Grandee Zhong, and sent Fan Li and Grandee Zheji to make peace and serve as hostages in Wu.

sentences.zh: 二歲而吳歸蠡。

translations.literal: After two years, Wu returned Li.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, Wu returned Li.

sentences.zh: 句踐自會稽歸七年，拊循其士民，欲用以報吳。

translations.literal: Seven years after Goujian returned from Kuaiji, he comforted and cared for his officers and people, intending to use them to avenge himself on Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years after Goujian returned from Kuaiji, he comforted and cared for his officers and people, intending to use them to avenge himself on Wu.

sentences.zh: 大夫逢同諫曰：「國新流亡，今乃復殷給，繕飾備利，吳必懼，懼則難必至。

translations.literal: Grandee Fengtong remonstrated: “The state has only recently returned from exile and ruin. If we now again become rich and well supplied, repair our equipment, and sharpen our preparations, Wu will certainly be afraid; if it is afraid, disaster will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Fengtong remonstrated: “The state has only recently returned from exile and ruin. If we now again become rich and well supplied, repair our equipment, and sharpen our preparations, Wu will certainly be afraid; if it is afraid, disaster will surely come.

sentences.zh: 且鷙鳥之擊也，必匿其形。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a fierce bird strikes, it certainly hides its form.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a fierce bird strikes, it certainly hides its form.

sentences.zh: 今夫吳兵加齊、晉，怨深於楚、越，名高天下，實害周室，德少而功多，必淫自矜。

translations.literal: Now Wu's troops press upon Qi and Jin. Its resentment runs deep with Chu and Yue. Its name is high in the world, but in substance it harms the Zhou royal house. Virtue is scant but merit is great. It will certainly grow insolent and self-conceited.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wu's troops press upon Qi and Jin. Its resentment runs deep with Chu and Yue. Its name is high in the world, but in substance it harms the Zhou royal house. Virtue is scant but merit is great. It will certainly grow insolent and self-conceited.

sentences.zh: 為越計，莫若結齊，親楚，附晉，以厚吳。

translations.literal: For Yue's plan, nothing is better than allying with Qi, befriending Chu, attaching to Jin, to keep Wu complacent.
translations.idiomatic: For Yue's plan, nothing is better than allying with Qi, befriending Chu, and attaching to Jin, so as to keep Wu complacent.

sentences.zh: 吳之志廣，必輕戰。

translations.literal: Wu's ambitions are broad. It will certainly fight rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's ambitions are broad. It will certainly fight rashly.

sentences.zh: 是我連其權，三國伐之，越承其弊，可克也。」

translations.literal: This will bind Wu’s strength. When the three states attack it and Yue takes advantage of its exhaustion, we can defeat it.”
translations.idiomatic: This will bind Wu’s strength. When the three states attack it and Yue takes advantage of its exhaustion, we can defeat it.”

sentences.zh: 句踐曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Gou Jian said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian said: 'Good.'

sentences.zh: 居二年，吳王將伐齊。

translations.literal: After two years, the Wu wang was about to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, the Wu king was about to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 子胥諫曰：「未可。

translations.literal: Wu Zixu remonstrated: “It is not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu remonstrated: “Not yet.

sentences.zh: 臣聞句踐食不重味，與百姓同苦樂。

translations.literal: I have heard that Gou Jian eats no repeated flavors and shares bitterness and joy with the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Gou Jian eats no repeated flavors and shares bitterness and joy with the common people.

sentences.zh: 此人不死，必為國患。

translations.literal: If this person does not die, he will certainly become a state calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If this person does not die, he will certainly become a state calamity.

sentences.zh: 吳有越，腹心之疾，齊與吳，疥癬也。

translations.literal: For Wu, Yue is a disease of the heart and belly; Qi is only scabies and ringworm.
translations.idiomatic: For Wu, Yue is a disease of the heart and belly; Qi is only scabies and ringworm.

sentences.zh: 願王釋齊先越。」

translations.literal: I hope the king will leave Qi aside and deal with Yue first.”
translations.idiomatic: I hope the king will leave Qi aside and deal with Yue first.”

sentences.zh: 吳王弗聽，遂伐齊，敗之艾陵，虜齊高、國以歸。

translations.literal: The Wu wang did not listen. He then attacked Qi, defeated them at Ai Ling, captured Qi Gao and Guo, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu king did not listen. He then attacked Qi, defeated them at Ai Ling, captured Gao and Guo of Qi, and returned.

sentences.zh: 讓子胥。

translations.literal: He reproached Zi Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He reproached Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 子胥曰：「王毋喜！」

translations.literal: Zi Xu said: 'Wang do not rejoice!'
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xu said: 'King, do not rejoice!'

sentences.zh: 王怒，子胥欲自殺，王聞而止之。

translations.literal: The wang was angered. Zi Xu desired suicide. The wang heard and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The king was angered. Zi Xu desired to commit suicide. The king heard and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 越大夫種曰：「臣觀吳王政驕矣，請試嘗之貸粟，以卜其事。」

translations.literal: Grandee Zhong of Yue said: “I observe that the king of Wu’s government has grown arrogant. Please let us test him by asking to borrow grain, so that we can divine how matters stand.”
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Zhong of Yue said: “I observe that the king of Wu’s government has grown arrogant. Please let us test him by asking to borrow grain, so that we can divine how matters stand.”

sentences.zh: 請貸，吳王欲與，子胥諫勿與，王遂與之，越乃私喜。

translations.literal: They requested to borrow. The Wu wang desired to give. Zi Xu admonished not to give. The wang then gave it. Yue then privately rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: They requested to borrow. The Wu king desired to give. Zi Xu admonished not to give. The king then gave it. Yue then privately rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 子胥言曰：「王不聽諫，後三年吳其墟乎！」

translations.literal: Wu Zixu said, “If the king does not listen to remonstrance, in three years Wu may be ruins!”
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu said, “If the king does not listen to remonstrance, in three years Wu may be ruins!”

sentences.zh: 太宰嚭聞之，乃數與子胥爭越議，因讒子胥曰：「伍員貌忠而實忍人，其父兄不顧，安能顧王？

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator Pi heard this and repeatedly disputed Yue policy with Wu Zixu. He then slandered Wu Zixu, saying: “Wu Yuan appears loyal, but in truth he is cruel. He did not care for his own father and elder brother; how can he care for the king?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator Pi heard this and repeatedly disputed Yue policy with Wu Zixu. He then slandered Wu Zixu, saying: “Wu Yuan appears loyal, but in truth he is cruel. He did not care for his own father and elder brother; how can he care for the king?

sentences.zh: 王前欲伐齊，員彊諫，已而有功，用是反怨王。

translations.literal: When the king previously wanted to attack Qi, Wu Yuan strongly remonstrated. After the campaign succeeded, he used this as a reason to resent the king.
translations.idiomatic: When the king previously wanted to attack Qi, Wu Yuan strongly remonstrated. After the campaign succeeded, he used this as a reason to resent the king.

sentences.zh: 王不備伍員，員必為亂。」

translations.literal: Wang not prepare Wu Yuan, Yuan certainly causes chaos.'
translations.idiomatic: If the king does not prepare for Wu Yuan, Yuan will certainly cause chaos.'

sentences.zh: 與逢同共謀，讒之王。

translations.literal: Together with Feng Tong they plotted and slandered to the wang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Feng Tong they plotted and slandered to the king.

sentences.zh: 王始不從，乃使子胥於齊，聞其託子於鮑氏，王乃大怒，曰：「伍員果欺寡人！」

translations.literal: Wang at first not followed, then sent Zi Xu to Qi, heard he entrusted son to Bao clan, wang then greatly angered, said: 'Wu Yuan indeed deceives I!'
translations.idiomatic: The king at first did not follow, then sent Zi Xu to Qi. He heard that Zi Xu had entrusted his son to the Bao clan. The king then became greatly angered and said: 'Wu Yuan indeed deceives me!'

sentences.zh: 役反，使人賜子胥屬鏤劍以自殺。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, the king sent someone to bestow on Wu Zixu the Zhulou sword, with which he was to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, the king sent someone to bestow on Wu Zixu the Zhulou sword, with which he was to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 子胥大笑曰：「我令而父霸，我又立若，若初欲分吳國半予我，我不受，已，今若反以讒誅我。

translations.literal: Zi Xu laughed loudly and said: 'I made your father hegemon, and I moreover established you. You at first wished to divide the Wu state in half and give it to me. I did not accept it. And now you instead use slander to execute me.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu laughed loudly and said: 'I made your father hegemon, and I moreover established you. You at first wished to divide the Wu state in half and give it to me. I did not accept it. And now you instead use slander to execute me.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，嗟乎，一人固不能獨立！」

translations.literal: Alas, alas—a lone man truly cannot succeed alone!'
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas—a lone man truly cannot succeed alone!'

sentences.zh: 報使者曰：「必取吾眼置吳東門，以觀越兵入也！」

translations.literal: He told the envoy, “You must take my eyes and place them on Wu’s eastern gate, so that I may watch the Yue army enter!”
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoy, “You must take my eyes and place them on Wu’s eastern gate, so that I may watch the Yue army enter!”

sentences.zh: 於是吳任嚭政。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu entrusted the government to Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wu entrusted the government to Pi.

sentences.zh: 居三年，句踐召范蠡曰：「吳已殺子胥，導諛者眾，可乎？」

translations.literal: After three years, Goujian summoned Fan Li and said, “Wu has already killed Zixu, and those who guide the king with flattery are many. Is the time right?”
translations.idiomatic: After three years, Goujian summoned Fan Li and said, “Wu has already killed Zixu, and those who guide the king with flattery are many. Is the time right?”

sentences.zh: 對曰：「未可。」

translations.literal: Fan Li replied, “Not yet.”
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li replied, “Not yet.”

sentences.zh: 至明年春，吳王北會諸侯於黃池，吳國精兵從王，惟獨老弱與太子留守。

translations.literal: By the next spring, the king of Wu went north to meet the feudal lords at Huangchi. Wu’s elite troops followed the king, leaving only the old, the weak, and the crown prince to defend the state.
translations.idiomatic: By the next spring, the king of Wu went north to meet the feudal lords at Huangchi. Wu’s elite troops followed the king, leaving only the old, the weak, and the crown prince to defend the state.

sentences.zh: 句踐復問范蠡，蠡曰「可矣」。

translations.literal: Goujian again asked Fan Li. Fan Li said, “Now it is possible.”
translations.idiomatic: Goujian again asked Fan Li. Fan Li said, “Now it is possible.”

sentences.zh: 乃發習流二千人，教士四萬人，君子六千人，諸御千人，伐吳。

translations.literal: He then sent two thousand trained naval men, forty thousand drilled soldiers, six thousand noble retainers, and one thousand royal attendants to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent two thousand trained naval men, forty thousand drilled soldiers, six thousand noble retainers, and one thousand royal attendants to attack Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳師敗，遂殺吳太子。

translations.literal: The Wu troops were defeated. They then killed the Wu crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu troops were defeated. They then killed the Wu crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吳告急於王，王方會諸侯於黃池，懼天下聞之，乃祕之。

translations.literal: Wu sent urgent word to its king, but the king was then meeting with the feudal lords at Huangchi. Fearing that all under heaven would hear of it, he kept the news secret.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent urgent word to its king, but the king was then meeting with the feudal lords at Huangchi. Fearing that all under heaven would hear of it, he kept the news secret.

sentences.zh: 吳王已盟黃池，乃使人厚禮以請成越。

translations.literal: After the king of Wu had concluded the covenant at Huangchi, he sent someone with generous gifts to request peace with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After the king of Wu had concluded the covenant at Huangchi, he sent someone with generous gifts to request peace with Yue.

sentences.zh: 越自度亦未能滅吳，乃與吳平。

translations.literal: Yue judged that it still could not destroy Wu, and so it made peace with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue judged that it still could not destroy Wu, and so it made peace with Wu.

sentences.zh: 其後四年，越復伐吳。

translations.literal: Four years later, Yue again attacked Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, Yue again attacked Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳士民罷弊，輕銳盡死於齊、晉。

translations.literal: Wu’s officers and people were exhausted and worn out, and all its light and elite troops had died in the wars against Qi and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s officers and people were exhausted and worn out, and all its light and elite troops had died in the wars against Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 而越大破吳，因而留圍之三年，吳師敗，越遂復棲吳王於姑蘇之山。

translations.literal: Yue then inflicted a great defeat on Wu, remained to besiege it for three years, and defeated the Wu army. Yue once again confined the king of Wu on Mount Gusu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then inflicted a great defeat on Wu, remained to besiege it for three years, and defeated the Wu army. Yue once again confined the king of Wu on Mount Gusu.

sentences.zh: 吳王使公孫雄肉袒膝行而前，請成越王曰：「孤臣夫差敢布腹心，異日嘗得罪於會稽，夫差不敢逆命，得與君王成以歸。

translations.literal: The king of Wu sent Gongsun Xiong, who bared his upper body and walked forward on his knees, to request peace from the king of Yue, saying: “Your orphaned servant Fuchai dares to lay bare his innermost thoughts. On a former day I offended at Kuaiji, but Fuchai did not dare defy the command and was allowed to make peace with Your Majesty and return.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Wu sent Gongsun Xiong, who bared his upper body and walked forward on his knees, to request peace from the king of Yue, saying: “Your orphaned servant Fuchai dares to lay bare his innermost thoughts. On a former day I offended at Kuaiji, but Fuchai did not dare defy the command and was allowed to make peace with Your Majesty and return.

sentences.zh: 今君王舉玉趾而誅孤臣，孤臣惟命是聽，意者亦欲如會稽之赦孤臣之罪乎？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty raises his jade feet to execute your orphaned servant, and your orphaned servant will obey your command. Perhaps you also wish to pardon your orphaned servant’s offense, as Wu pardoned Yue at Kuaiji?”
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty raises his jade feet to execute your orphaned servant, and your orphaned servant will obey your command. Perhaps you also wish to pardon your orphaned servant’s offense, as Wu pardoned Yue at Kuaiji?”

sentences.zh: 句踐不忍，欲許之。

translations.literal: Goujian could not bear it and wanted to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian could not bear it and wanted to agree.

sentences.zh: 范蠡曰：「會稽之事，天以越賜吳，吳不取。

translations.literal: Fan Li said: “In the affair at Kuaiji, Heaven gave Yue to Wu, but Wu did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li said: “In the affair at Kuaiji, Heaven gave Yue to Wu, but Wu did not take it.

sentences.zh: 今天以吳賜越，越其可逆天乎？

translations.literal: Now Heaven gives Wu to Yue. How can Yue defy Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven gives Wu to Yue. How can Yue defy Heaven?

sentences.zh: 且夫君王蚤朝晏罷，非為吳邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty rose early and retired late; was it not for Wu?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty rose early and retired late; was it not for Wu?

sentences.zh: 謀之二十二年，一旦而棄之，可乎？

translations.literal: You planned this for twenty-two years. Can you cast it aside in a single morning?
translations.idiomatic: You planned this for twenty-two years. Can you cast it aside in a single morning?

sentences.zh: 且夫天與弗取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Heaven gives something and one does not take it, one instead receives the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Heaven gives something and one does not take it, one instead receives the blame.

sentences.zh: 『伐柯者其則不遠』，君忘會稽之蚯？」

translations.literal: The saying goes, ‘When cutting an axe handle, the model is not far away.’ Has Your Majesty forgotten the humiliation of Kuaiji?”
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, ‘When cutting an axe handle, the model is not far away.’ Has Your Majesty forgotten the humiliation of Kuaiji?”

sentences.zh: 句踐曰：「吾欲聽子言，吾不忍其使者。」

translations.literal: Goujian said: “I want to follow your words, but I cannot bear to look at his envoy.”
translations.idiomatic: Goujian said: “I want to follow your words, but I cannot bear to look at his envoy.”

sentences.zh: 范蠡乃鼓進兵，曰：「王已屬政於執事，使者去，不者且得罪。」

translations.literal: Fan Li then beat the drums and advanced the troops, saying: “The king has already entrusted the government to his officers. Envoy, leave. If you do not, you will be guilty.”
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li then beat the drums and advanced the troops, saying: “The king has already entrusted the government to his officers. Envoy, leave. If you do not, you will be guilty.”

sentences.zh: 吳使者泣而去。

translations.literal: The Wu envoy wept and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu envoy wept and departed.

sentences.zh: 句踐憐之，乃使人謂吳王曰：「吾置王甬東，君百家。」

translations.literal: Goujian pitied him and sent someone to tell the king of Wu: “I will settle the king east of Yong and let him rule a hundred households.”
translations.idiomatic: Goujian pitied him and sent someone to tell the king of Wu: “I will settle the king east of Yong and let him rule a hundred households.”

sentences.zh: 吳王謝曰：「吾老矣，不能事君王！」

translations.literal: The king of Wu declined, saying: “I am old. I cannot serve Your Majesty!”
translations.idiomatic: The king of Wu declined, saying: “I am old. I cannot serve Your Majesty!”

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: He then committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He then committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 乃蔽其面，曰：「吾無面以見子胥也！」

translations.literal: He then covered his face and said: “I have no face with which to see Zixu!”
translations.idiomatic: He then covered his face and said: “I have no face with which to see Zixu!”

sentences.zh: 越王乃葬吳王而誅太宰嚭。

translations.literal: The king of Yue then buried the king of Wu and executed the Grand Administrator Pi.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yue then buried the king of Wu and executed the Grand Administrator Pi.

sentences.zh: 句踐已平吳，乃以兵北渡淮，與齊、晉諸侯會於徐州，致貢於周。

translations.literal: After Goujian had pacified Wu, he led his troops north across the Huai and met the feudal lords of Qi and Jin at Xuzhou, presenting tribute to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Goujian had pacified Wu, he led his troops north across the Huai and met the feudal lords of Qi and Jin at Xuzhou, presenting tribute to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周元王使人賜句踐胙，命為伯。

translations.literal: King Yuan of Zhou sent someone to grant Goujian sacrificial meat and appoint him hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: King Yuan of Zhou sent someone to grant Goujian sacrificial meat and appoint him hegemon.

sentences.zh: 句踐已去，渡淮南，以淮上地與楚，歸吳所侵宋地於宋，與魯泗東方百里。

translations.literal: After Goujian departed, he crossed south of the Huai, gave the lands along the Huai to Chu, returned the lands Wu had seized from Song to Song, and gave Lu a hundred li east of the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: After Goujian departed, he crossed south of the Huai, gave the lands along the Huai to Chu, returned the lands Wu had seized from Song to Song, and gave Lu a hundred li east of the Si River.

sentences.zh: 當是時，越兵橫行於江、淮東，諸侯畢賀，號稱霸王。

translations.literal: At that time, Yue troops ranged freely east of the Yangtze and Huai. All the feudal lords congratulated him, and he was styled hegemon-king.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Yue troops ranged freely east of the Yangtze and Huai. All the feudal lords congratulated him, and he was styled hegemon-king.

sentences.zh: 范蠡遂去，自齊遺大夫種書曰：「蜚鳥盡，良弓藏；

translations.literal: Fan Li then left. From Qi he sent Grandee Zhong a letter, saying: “When the flying birds are gone, the fine bow is stored away;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li then left. From Qi he sent Grandee Zhong a letter, saying: “When the flying birds are gone, the fine bow is stored away;

sentences.zh: 狡兔死，走狗烹。

translations.literal: when the cunning rabbit is dead, the running hound is cooked.
translations.idiomatic: when the cunning rabbit is dead, the running hound is cooked.

sentences.zh: 越王為人長頸鳥喙，可與共患難，不可與共樂。

translations.literal: The king of Yue has a long neck and a bird’s beak. One can share hardship and danger with him, but not joy.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yue has a long neck and a bird’s beak. One can share hardship and danger with him, but not joy.

sentences.zh: 子何不去？」

translations.literal: Why do you not leave?”
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not leave?”

sentences.zh: 種見書，稱病不朝。

translations.literal: When Zhong saw the letter, he claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong saw the letter, he claimed illness and did not attend court.

sentences.zh: 人或讒種且作亂，越王乃賜種劍曰：「子教寡人伐吳七術，寡人用其三而敗吳，其四在子，子為我從先王試之。」

translations.literal: Someone slandered Zhong, saying that he was about to start a rebellion. The king of Yue then bestowed a sword on Zhong and said: “You taught me seven strategies for attacking Wu. I used three of them and defeated Wu; the remaining four are still with you. Follow the former king and test them for me.”
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Zhong, saying that he was about to start a rebellion. The king of Yue then bestowed a sword on Zhong and said: “You taught me seven strategies for attacking Wu. I used three of them and defeated Wu; the remaining four are still with you. Follow the former king and test them for me.”

sentences.zh: 種遂自殺。

translations.literal: Zhong then committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 句踐卒，子王鼫與立。

translations.literal: Goujian died, and his son King Shuyu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian died, and his son King Shuyu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王鼫與卒，子王不壽立。

translations.literal: King Shuyu died, and his son King Bushou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: King Shuyu died, and his son King Bushou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王不壽卒，子王翁立。

translations.literal: Wang Bushou died. His son Wang Weng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bushou died. His son Wang Weng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王翁卒，子王翳立。

translations.literal: Wang Weng died. His son Wang Yi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weng died. His son Wang Yi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王翳卒，子王之侯立。

translations.literal: Wang Yi died. His son Wang Zhihou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi died. His son Wang Zhihou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王之侯卒，子王無彊立。

translations.literal: Wang Zhihou died. His son Wang Wuqiang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhihou died. His son Wang Wuqiang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王無彊時，越興師北伐齊，西伐楚，與中國爭彊。

translations.literal: During Wang Wu Qiang's time, Yue raised troops to attack Qi north and Chu west, contending for strength with the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Wu Qiang's time, Yue raised troops to attack Qi in the north and Chu in the west, contending for strength with the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 當楚威王之時，越北伐齊，齊威王使人說越王曰：「越不伐楚，大不王，小不伯。

translations.literal: At the time of King Wei of Chu, Yue attacked Qi in the north. King Wei of Qi sent someone to persuade the king of Yue, saying: “If Yue does not attack Chu, it will neither become great enough to be kingly nor lesser enough to be hegemonic.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of King Wei of Chu, Yue attacked Qi in the north. King Wei of Qi sent someone to persuade the king of Yue, saying: “If Yue does not attack Chu, it will neither become great enough to be kingly nor lesser enough to be hegemonic.

sentences.zh: 圖越之所為不伐楚者，為不得晉也。

translations.literal: Consider what Yue does by not attacking Chu - it is because it cannot obtain Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Consider what Yue does by not attacking Chu—it is because it cannot obtain the state of Jin.

sentences.zh: 韓、魏固不攻楚。

translations.literal: Han and Wei certainly will not attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei certainly will not attack Chu.

sentences.zh: 韓之攻楚，覆其軍，殺其將，則葉、陽翟危；

translations.literal: Han attack Chu, overturn its army, kill its general, then Ye, Yang Di dangerous;
translations.idiomatic: If Han attacks Chu, overturns its army, and kills its general, then the cities of Ye and Yang Di will be in danger;

sentences.zh: 魏亦覆其軍，殺其將，則陳、上蔡不安。

translations.literal: If Wei also overturns its army and kills its general, then Chen and Shang Cai will not be peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei also overturns its army and kills its general, then the cities of Chen and Shang Cai will not be peaceful.

sentences.zh: 故二晉之事越也，不至於覆軍殺將，馬汗之力不效。

translations.literal: Therefore, when the two Jin states serve Yue, they will not go so far as to overthrow armies and kill generals; even the effort that makes horses sweat will not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, when the two Jin states serve Yue, they will not go so far as to overthrow armies and kill generals; even the effort that makes horses sweat will not be applied.

sentences.zh: 所重於得晉者何也？」

translations.literal: What value in obtaining Jin?'
translations.idiomatic: What is the value in obtaining Jin?'

sentences.zh: 越王曰：「所求於晉者，不至頓刃接兵，而況于攻城圍邑乎？

translations.literal: The king of Yue said: “What we seek from Jin does not require clashing blades or joining battle, still less attacking cities and besieging towns.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yue said: “What we seek from Jin does not require clashing blades or joining battle, still less attacking cities and besieging towns.

sentences.zh: 願魏以聚大梁之下，願齊之試兵南陽莒地，以聚常、郯之境，則方城之外不南，淮、泗之閒不東，商、於、析、酈、宗胡之地，夏路以左，不足以備秦，江南、泗上不足以待越矣。

translations.literal: I want Wei to gather beneath Daliang. I want Qi to test its troops in Nanyang and the lands of Ju, gathering at the borders of Chang and Tan. Then the territory beyond Fangcheng will not move south, the region between the Huai and Si will not move east, the lands of Shang, Yu, Xi, Li, and Zonghu to the left of the Xia road will be insufficient to prepare against Qin, and Jiangnan and the Si River region will be insufficient to wait for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: I want Wei to gather beneath Daliang. I want Qi to test its troops in Nanyang and the lands of Ju, gathering at the borders of Chang and Tan. Then the territory beyond Fangcheng will not move south, the region between the Huai and Si will not move east, the lands of Shang, Yu, Xi, Li, and Zonghu to the left of the Xia road will be insufficient to prepare against Qin, and Jiangnan and the Si River region will be insufficient to wait for Yue.

sentences.zh: 則齊、秦、韓、魏得志於楚也，是二晉不戰分地，不耕而穫之。

translations.literal: Then Qi, Qin, Han, and Wei will realize their ambitions against Chu. The two Jin states will divide territory without fighting and harvest without plowing.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qi, Qin, Han, and Wei will realize their ambitions against Chu. The two Jin states will divide territory without fighting and harvest without plowing.

sentences.zh: 不此之為，而頓刃於河山之閒以為齊秦用，所待者如此其失計，柰何其以此王也！」

translations.literal: If they do not do this, but instead clash blades between the rivers and mountains to be used by Qi and Qin, what they await is such a mistaken plan. How could they use this to become kings?”
translations.idiomatic: If they do not do this, but instead clash blades between the rivers and mountains to be used by Qi and Qin, what they await is such a mistaken plan. How could they use this to become kings?”

sentences.zh: 齊使者曰：「幸也越之不亡也！

translations.literal: Qi envoy said: 'Fortunate Yue not perished!
translations.idiomatic: The Qi envoy said: 'It is fortunate that Yue has not perished!

sentences.zh: 吾不貴其用智之如目，見豪毛而不見其睫也。

translations.literal: I do not value the use of wisdom that resembles the eye: it can see fine hairs but cannot see its own eyelashes.
translations.idiomatic: I do not value the use of wisdom that resembles the eye: it can see fine hairs but cannot see its own eyelashes.

sentences.zh: 今王知晉之失計，而不自知越之過，是目論也。

translations.literal: Now the king knows Jin's mistaken plan, but does not know Yue's own fault. This is judging by the eye alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now the king knows Jin's mistaken plan, but does not know Yue's own fault. This is judging by the eye alone.

sentences.zh: 王所待於晉者，非有馬汗之力也，又非可與合軍連和也，將待之以分楚眾也。

translations.literal: What the king awaits from Jin is not the labor of sweating horses, nor can Jin join armies and make a linked alliance with him; he is waiting for it to divide the Chu forces.
translations.idiomatic: What the king awaits from Jin is not the labor of sweating horses, nor can Jin join armies and make a linked alliance with him; he is waiting for it to divide the Chu forces.

sentences.zh: 今楚眾已分，何待於晉？」

translations.literal: Now Chu masses already divided, what await from Jin?'
translations.idiomatic: Now that Chu's masses are already divided, what do you await from Jin?'

sentences.zh: 越王曰：「柰何？」

translations.literal: Yue wang said: 'What to do?'
translations.idiomatic: The Yue king said: 'What is to be done?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「楚三大夫張九軍，北圍曲沃、於中，以至無假之關者三千七百里，景翠之軍北聚魯、齊、南陽，分有大此者乎？

translations.literal: He said: “Chu’s three grandees have spread out nine armies. In the north they surround Quwo and Yuzhong, reaching as far as the Wujia Pass, a distance of three thousand seven hundred li. Jing Cui’s army gathers in the north at Lu, Qi, and Nanyang. Could the division be any greater than this?
translations.idiomatic: He said: “Chu’s three grandees have spread out nine armies. In the north they surround Quwo and Yuzhong, reaching as far as the Wujia Pass, a distance of three thousand seven hundred li. Jing Cui’s army gathers in the north at Lu, Qi, and Nanyang. Could the division be any greater than this?

sentences.zh: 且王之所求者，鬬晉楚也；

translations.literal: Moreover, wang what seeks, fight Jin Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what the king seeks is to make Jin and Chu fight;

sentences.zh: 晉楚不鬬，越兵不起，是知二五而不知十也。

translations.literal: If Jin and Chu do not fight, Yue’s troops will not rise. This is knowing two and five, but not knowing ten.
translations.idiomatic: If Jin and Chu do not fight, Yue’s troops will not rise. This is knowing two and five, but not knowing ten.

sentences.zh: 此時不攻楚，臣以是知越大不王，小不伯。

translations.literal: If Yue does not attack Chu at this moment, I know that Yue will neither become great enough to be kingly nor lesser enough to be hegemonic.
translations.idiomatic: If Yue does not attack Chu at this moment, I know that Yue will neither become great enough to be kingly nor lesser enough to be hegemonic.

sentences.zh: 復讎、龐、長沙，楚之粟也；

translations.literal: Fuqiu, Pang, and Changsha are Chu’s granaries;
translations.idiomatic: Fuqiu, Pang, and Changsha are Chu’s granaries;

sentences.zh: 竟澤陵，楚之材也。

translations.literal: Jingzeling is Chu’s timberland.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzeling is Chu’s timberland.

sentences.zh: 越窺兵通無假之關，此四邑者不上貢事於郢矣。

translations.literal: If Yue’s troops probe through to the Wujia Pass, these four cities will no longer send tribute or service to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: If Yue’s troops probe through to the Wujia Pass, these four cities will no longer send tribute or service to Ying.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，圖王不王，其敝可以伯。

translations.literal: I have heard that if one plans for kingship but does not become king, the setback can still allow one to become hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that if one plans for kingship but does not become king, the setback can still allow one to become hegemon.

sentences.zh: 然而不伯者，王道失也。

translations.literal: But if one does not even become hegemon, the kingly Way has been lost.
translations.idiomatic: But if one does not even become hegemon, the kingly Way has been lost.

sentences.zh: 故願大王之轉攻楚也。」

translations.literal: Therefore, I hope Your Majesty will turn and attack Chu.”
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, I hope Your Majesty will turn and attack Chu.”

sentences.zh: 於是越遂釋齊而伐楚。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue then released Qi and attacked Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yue then released Qi and attacked Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚威王興兵而伐之，大敗越，殺王無彊，盡取笔吳地至浙江，北破齊於徐州。

translations.literal: King Wei of Chu raised troops and attacked Yue. He dealt Yue a great defeat, killed King Wuqiang, took all the former Wu lands as far as the Zhejiang, and in the north defeated Qi at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Wei of Chu raised troops and attacked Yue. He dealt Yue a great defeat, killed King Wuqiang, took all the former Wu lands as far as the Zhejiang, and in the north defeated Qi at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 而越以此散，諸族子爭立，或為王，或為君，濱於江南海上，服朝於楚。

translations.literal: Because of this, Yue scattered. The various sons of its clans contended to establish themselves, some as kings and some as lords. Along the Jiangnan coast, they submitted and paid court to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, Yue scattered. The various sons of its clans contended to establish themselves, some as kings and some as lords. Along the Jiangnan coast, they submitted and paid court to Chu.

sentences.zh: 後七世，至閩君搖，佐諸侯平秦。

translations.literal: Seven generations later came Yao, Lord of Min, who assisted the feudal lords in pacifying Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later came Yao, Lord of Min, who assisted the feudal lords in pacifying Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝復以搖為越王，以奉越後。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Han again made Yao king of Yue, to maintain the Yue line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Han again made Yao king of Yue, to maintain the Yue line.

sentences.zh: 東越，閩君，皆其後也。

translations.literal: Eastern Yue and the Lords of Min were all his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yue and the Lords of Min were all his descendants.

sentences.zh: 范蠡事越王句踐，既苦身力，與句踐深謀二十餘年，竟滅吳，報會稽之恥，北渡兵於淮以臨齊、晉，號令中國，以尊周室，句踐以霸，而范蠡稱上將軍。

translations.literal: Fan Li served King Goujian of Yue, strained his body and strength, and planned deeply with Goujian for more than twenty years. In the end they destroyed Wu, avenged the shame of Kuaiji, moved their troops north across the Huai to confront Qi and Jin, issued commands to the Central States in order to honor the Zhou royal house, and Goujian became hegemon, while Fan Li was called Supreme General.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li served King Goujian of Yue, strained his body and strength, and planned deeply with Goujian for more than twenty years. In the end they destroyed Wu, avenged the shame of Kuaiji, moved their troops north across the Huai to confront Qi and Jin, issued commands to the Central States in order to honor the Zhou royal house, and Goujian became hegemon, while Fan Li was called Supreme General.

sentences.zh: 還反國，范蠡以為大名之下，難以久居，且句踐為人可與同患，難與處安，為書辭句踐曰：「臣聞主憂臣勞，主辱臣死。

translations.literal: After returning to the state, Fan Li thought that it was hard to remain long beneath a great reputation. Moreover, Goujian was the kind of man with whom one could share hardship, but not peace. He wrote a letter resigning from Goujian, saying: “I have heard that when the lord is anxious, the minister toils; when the lord is humiliated, the minister dies.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the state, Fan Li thought that it was hard to remain long beneath a great reputation. Moreover, Goujian was a man with whom one could share hardship, but not peace. He wrote a letter resigning from Goujian, saying: “I have heard that when the lord is anxious, the minister toils; when the lord is humiliated, the minister dies.

sentences.zh: 昔者君王辱於會稽，所以不死，為此事也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was humiliated at Kuaiji, the reason I did not die was for the sake of this affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was humiliated at Kuaiji, the reason I did not die was for the sake of this affair.

sentences.zh: 今既以雪恥，臣請從會稽之誅。」

translations.literal: Now that the shame has been avenged, I request to submit to the punishment of Kuaiji.”
translations.idiomatic: Now that the shame has been avenged, I request to submit to the punishment of Kuaiji.”

sentences.zh: 句踐曰：「孤將與子分國而有之。

translations.literal: Goujian said, “I will divide the state with you and let you possess it with me.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian said, “I will divide the state with you and let you possess it with me.

sentences.zh: 不然，將加誅于子。」

translations.literal: If you refuse, I will punish you.”
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, I will punish you.”

sentences.zh: 范蠡曰：「君行令，臣行意。」

translations.literal: Fan Li said: 'Lord execute commands, minister execute intentions.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li said: 'The lord executes commands, and the minister executes intentions.'

sentences.zh: 乃裝其輕寶珠玉，自與其私徒屬乘舟浮海以行，終不反。

translations.literal: He then packed his light treasures of pearls and jade, himself with his private followers rode a boat and floated on the sea to go. He finally did not return.
translations.idiomatic: He then packed his light treasures of pearls and jade, and himself with his private followers rode a boat and floated on the sea to go. He finally did not return.

sentences.zh: 於是句踐表會稽山以為范蠡奉邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gou Jian registered Mount Kuaiji as Fan Li's fief for revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gou Jian registered Mount Kuaiji as Fan Li's fief for revenue.

sentences.zh: 范蠡浮海出齊，變姓名，自謂鴟夷子皮，耕于海畔，苦身戮力，父子治產。

translations.literal: Fan Li floated on the sea and exited to Qi. He changed his name and called himself Chi Yi Zi Pi. He farmed at the seashore, tormented his body and exerted strength. Father and son managed property.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li floated on the sea and exited to Qi. He changed his name and called himself Chi Yi Zi Pi. He farmed at the seashore, tormented his body and exerted strength. Father and son managed property.

sentences.zh: 居無幾何，致產數十萬。

translations.literal: He resided not long before obtaining property of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He resided not long before obtaining property of several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 齊人聞其賢，以為相。

translations.literal: The Qi people heard of his worth and made him prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi people heard of his worth and made him prime minister.

sentences.zh: 范蠡喟然嘆曰：「居家則致千金，居官則至卿相，此布衣之極也。

translations.literal: Fan Li sighed said: 'Reside home then obtain thousand gold, reside office then reach minister chancellor, this commoner extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li sighed and said: 'To reside at home then obtain a thousand gold, to reside in office then reach minister and chancellor—this is the extreme for a commoner.

sentences.zh: 久受尊名，不祥。」

translations.literal: Long receive honored name, not auspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: To long receive an honored name is not auspicious.'

sentences.zh: 乃歸相印，盡散其財，以分與知友鄉黨，而懷其重寶，閒行以去，止于陶，以為此天下之中，交易有無之路通，為生可以致富矣。

translations.literal: He then returned the prime minister seal and completely scattered his wealth to divide with known friends and village parties. But he carried his heavy treasures and secretly went away, stopping at Tao. He thought this was the world's center where trade and commerce roads connected, and doing business could make one rich.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned the prime minister seal and completely scattered his wealth to divide with known friends and village parties. But he carried his heavy treasures and secretly went away, stopping at Tao. He thought this was the world's center where trade and commerce roads connected, and doing business could make one rich.

sentences.zh: 於是自謂陶朱公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he called himself Tao Zhu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he called himself Tao Zhu Gong.

sentences.zh: 復約要父子耕畜，廢居，候時轉物，逐什一之利。

translations.literal: He again made an agreement with father and son to farm and raise livestock, hoard goods and sell when the time was right, and pursue a ten-percent profit.
translations.idiomatic: He again made an agreement with father and son to farm and raise livestock, hoard goods and sell when the time was right, and pursue a ten-percent profit.

sentences.zh: 居無何，則致貲累巨萬。

translations.literal: He resided not long before obtaining wealth that accumulated to great tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He resided not long before obtaining wealth that accumulated to great tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 天下稱陶朱公。

translations.literal: The world called him Tao Zhu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The world called him Tao Zhu Gong.

sentences.zh: 朱公居陶，生少子。

translations.literal: Zhu Gong resided in Tao and gave birth to a young son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong resided in Tao and had a young son.

sentences.zh: 少子及壯，而朱公中男殺人，囚於楚。

translations.literal: The young son reached adulthood, but Zhu Gong's middle son killed a person and was imprisoned in Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The young son reached adulthood, but Zhu Gong's middle son killed a person and was imprisoned in Chu.

sentences.zh: 朱公曰：「殺人而死，職也。

translations.literal: Zhu Gong said: 'To kill a person and die for it is one's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong said: 'To kill a person and die for it is one's duty.

sentences.zh: 然吾聞千金之子不死於市。」

translations.literal: However, I heard thousand gold son not die at market.'
translations.idiomatic: However, I have heard that the son of a thousand gold does not die at the market.'

sentences.zh: 告其少子往視之。

translations.literal: He told his young son to go see him.
translations.idiomatic: He told his young son to go see him.

sentences.zh: 乃裝黃金千溢，置褐器中，載以一牛車。

translations.literal: He then packed a thousand yi of yellow gold, placed it in a coarse vessel, and loaded it with one ox cart.
translations.idiomatic: He then packed a thousand yi of yellow gold, placed it in a coarse vessel, and loaded it with one ox cart.

sentences.zh: 且遣其少子，朱公長男固請欲行，朱公不聽。

translations.literal: He moreover sent his young son. Zhu Gong's eldest son firmly requested to go, but Zhu Gong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He moreover sent his young son. However, Zhu Gong's eldest son firmly requested to go, but Zhu Gong did not listen to the request.

sentences.zh: 長男曰：「家有長子曰家督，今弟有罪，大人不遣，乃遺少弟，是吾不肖。」

translations.literal: Eldest male said: 'Family has eldest son called family supervisor, now younger brother has crime, great person not send, then send young brother, this my unworthy.'
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son said: 'The family has an eldest son called the family supervisor. Now my younger brother has a crime. The great person does not send me, but instead sends the young brother. This shows I am unworthy.'

sentences.zh: 欲自殺。

translations.literal: He desired to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He desired to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 其母為言曰：「今遣少子，未必能生中子也，而先空亡長男，柰何？」

translations.literal: His mother for spoke said: 'Now send young son, perhaps not able save middle son, but first vainly lose eldest male, what to do?'
translations.idiomatic: His mother spoke on his behalf, saying: 'If we now send the youngest son, we may not be able to save the middle son, and we will first lose the eldest son for nothing. What should we do?'

sentences.zh: 朱公不得已而遣長子，為一封書遺故所善莊生。

translations.literal: Zhu Gong had no choice but to send the eldest son. He made one sealed letter to send to his former friend Zhuang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong had no choice but to send the eldest son. He made one sealed letter to send to his former friend Zhuang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 曰：「至則進千金于莊生所，聽其所為，慎無與爭事。」

translations.literal: Said: 'Arrive then advance thousand gold at Zhuang Sheng place, listen his doings, careful not with contend affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'When you arrive, advance a thousand gold at Zhuang Sheng's place. Listen to what he does, and be careful not to contend with him over affairs.'

sentences.zh: 長男既行，亦自私齎數百金。

translations.literal: The eldest son already went. He also privately carried several hundred gold himself.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son already went. He also privately carried several hundred gold himself.

sentences.zh: 至楚，莊生家負郭，披藜藋到門，居甚貧。

translations.literal: He arrived in Chu. Zhuang Sheng's home backed the outer wall. He brushed through thorns and thistles to the door. He resided very poorly.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived in Chu. Zhuang Sheng's home backed the outer wall. He brushed through thorns and thistles to the door. He resided very poorly.

sentences.zh: 然長男發書進千金，如其父言。

translations.literal: However, the eldest son opened the letter and advanced a thousand gold, as his father said.
translations.idiomatic: However, the eldest son opened the letter and advanced a thousand gold, as his father said.

sentences.zh: 莊生曰：「可疾去矣，慎毋留！

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng said: 'Can quickly go, careful not stay!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng said: 'You can quickly go. Be careful not to stay!

sentences.zh: 即弟出，勿問所以然。」

translations.literal: When younger brother released, not ask reason.'
translations.idiomatic: When your younger brother is released, do not ask the reason.'

sentences.zh: 長男既去，不過莊生而私留，以其私齎獻遺楚國貴人用事者。

translations.literal: The eldest son already went. He did not pass Zhuang Sheng but privately stayed, offering and presenting what he privately carried to Chu state's nobles who handled affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son already went. He did not pass Zhuang Sheng but privately stayed, offering and presenting what he privately carried to the Chu state's nobles who handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 莊生雖居窮閻，然以廉直聞於國，自楚王以下皆師尊之。

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng though resided in a poor alley, however he was heard in the state for incorruptibility and straightness. From the Chu wang below, all honored him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng though resided in a poor alley, however he was heard in the state for incorruptibility and straightness. From the Chu king below, all honored him as teacher.

sentences.zh: 及朱公進金，非有意受也，欲以成事後復歸之以為信耳。

translations.literal: When Zhu Gong advanced the gold, he did not intentionally receive it. He desired to complete the affairs and then return it as trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Gong advanced the gold, he did not intentionally receive it. He desired to complete the affairs and then return it as a sign of trust.

sentences.zh: 故金至，謂其婦曰：「此朱公之金。

translations.literal: Therefore, gold arrived, told his wife said: 'This Zhu Gong gold.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, when the gold arrived, he told his wife, saying: 'This is Zhu Gong's gold.

sentences.zh: 有如病不宿誡，後復歸，勿動。」

translations.literal: If, as with an illness not cured in one night, I later return it—do not touch it.'
translations.idiomatic: If, as with an illness not cured in one night, I later return it—do not touch it.'

sentences.zh: 而朱公長男不知其意，以為殊無短長也。

translations.literal: But Zhu Gong's eldest son did not know his intention. He thought there was no hope in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhu Gong's eldest son did not know his intention. He thought there was no hope in the matter.

sentences.zh: 莊生閒時入見楚王，言「某星宿某，此則害於楚」。

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng leisure time entered saw Chu wang, spoke 'some star lodges some, this then harms Chu'.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng in his leisure time entered and saw the Chu king, speaking: 'A certain star lodges in a certain place. This then harms Chu.'

sentences.zh: 楚王素信莊生，曰：「今為柰何？」

translations.literal: Chu wang usually trusted Zhuang Sheng, said: 'Now what to do?'
translations.idiomatic: The Chu king usually trusted Zhuang Sheng and said: 'What should be done now?'

sentences.zh: 莊生曰：「獨以德為可以除之。」

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng said: 'Only with virtue can remove it.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng said: 'Only with virtue can one remove it.'

sentences.zh: 楚王曰：「生休矣，寡人將行之。」

translations.literal: Chu wang said: 'Sheng rest, I will carry it out.'
translations.idiomatic: The Chu king said: 'Sheng, rest. I will carry it out.'

sentences.zh: 王乃使使者封三錢之府。

translations.literal: The wang then sent an envoy to seal the three money treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: The king then sent an envoy to seal the three money treasuries.

sentences.zh: 楚貴人驚告朱公長男曰：「王且赦。」

translations.literal: Chu nobles alarmed told Zhu Gong eldest male said: 'Wang about to pardon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Chu nobles were alarmed and told Zhu Gong's eldest son, saying: 'The king is about to pardon.'

sentences.zh: 曰：「何以也？」

translations.literal: Said: 'Why?'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'Why is this?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「每王且赦，常封三錢之府。

translations.literal: Said: 'Whenever wang about to pardon, always seals three money treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'Whenever the king is about to pardon, he always seals the three money treasuries.

sentences.zh: 昨暮王使使封之。」

translations.literal: Last evening wang sent envoy sealed them.'
translations.idiomatic: Last evening the king sent an envoy and sealed them.'

sentences.zh: 朱公長男以為赦，弟固當出也，重千金虛棄莊生，無所為也，乃復見莊生。

translations.literal: Zhu Gong’s eldest son thought this meant a pardon had been issued and that his younger brother would certainly be released. He grudged the thousand gold pieces he had left with Zhuang Sheng for nothing, so he went to see Zhuang Sheng again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong’s eldest son thought this meant a pardon had been issued and that his younger brother would certainly be released. He grudged the thousand gold pieces he had left with Zhuang Sheng for nothing, so he went to see Zhuang Sheng again.

sentences.zh: 莊生驚曰：「若不去邪？」

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng startled said: 'You not go?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng was startled and said: 'Have you not gone?'

sentences.zh: 長男曰：「固未也。

translations.literal: The eldest son said, “Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son said, “Not yet.

sentences.zh: 初為事弟，弟今議自赦，故辭生去。」

translations.literal: At first I came because of my younger brother’s case. Now my younger brother is apparently to be pardoned, so I have come to bid you farewell before leaving.”
translations.idiomatic: At first I came because of my younger brother’s case. Now my younger brother is apparently to be pardoned, so I have come to bid you farewell before leaving.”

sentences.zh: 莊生知其意欲復得其金，曰：「若自入室取金。」

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng knew that he meant to recover his gold and said, “Go into the room yourself and take the gold.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng knew that he meant to recover his gold and said, “Go into the room yourself and take the gold.”

sentences.zh: 長男即自入室取金持去，獨自歡幸。

translations.literal: The eldest son immediately went into the room himself, took the gold, and left with it, privately rejoicing in his good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son immediately went into the room himself, took the gold, and left with it, privately rejoicing in his good fortune.

sentences.zh: 莊生羞為兒子所賣，乃入見楚王曰：「臣前言某星事，王言欲以修德報之。

translations.literal: Zhuang Sheng was ashamed at having been betrayed by the young man, so he went in to see the King of Chu and said: “Earlier I spoke to Your Majesty about the matter of a certain star, and Your Majesty said that you wished to respond by cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Sheng was ashamed at having been betrayed by the young man, so he went in to see the King of Chu and said: “Earlier I spoke to Your Majesty about the matter of a certain star, and Your Majesty said that you wished to respond by cultivating virtue.

sentences.zh: 今臣出，道路皆言陶之富人朱公之子殺人囚楚，其家多持金錢賂王左右，故王非能恤楚國而赦，乃以朱公子故也。」

translations.literal: Now when I went out, everyone on the road was saying that the son of Zhu Gong, a rich man of Tao, had killed someone and been imprisoned in Chu; that his family had brought much gold and money to bribe Your Majesty’s attendants; and that Your Majesty was issuing a pardon not out of concern for the state of Chu, but because of Zhu Gong’s son.”
translations.idiomatic: Now when I went out, everyone on the road was saying that the son of Zhu Gong, a rich man of Tao, had killed someone and been imprisoned in Chu; that his family had brought much gold and money to bribe Your Majesty’s attendants; and that Your Majesty was issuing a pardon not out of concern for the state of Chu, but because of Zhu Gong’s son.”

sentences.zh: 楚王大怒曰：「寡人雖不德耳，柰何以朱公之子故而施惠乎！」

translations.literal: The King of Chu was furious and said: “Though I lack virtue, how could I bestow favor merely because of Zhu Gong’s son?”
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chu was furious and said: “Though I lack virtue, how could I bestow favor merely because of Zhu Gong’s son?”

sentences.zh: 令論殺朱公子，明日遂下赦令。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhu Gong’s son tried and executed, and the next day he issued the pardon order.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhu Gong’s son tried and executed, and the next day he issued the pardon order.

sentences.zh: 朱公長男竟持其弟喪歸。

translations.literal: Zhu Gong's eldest son finally held his younger brother's funeral and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong's eldest son finally held his younger brother's funeral and returned.

sentences.zh: 至，其母及邑人盡哀之，唯朱公獨笑，曰：「吾固知必殺其弟也！

translations.literal: Arrived, his mother and city people all grieved him, only Zhu Gong alone laughed, said: 'I certainly knew would kill his younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, his mother and the city people all grieved for him. Only Zhu Gong alone laughed and said: 'I certainly knew he would kill his younger brother!

sentences.zh: 彼非不愛其弟，顧有所不能忍者也。

translations.literal: He did not not love his younger brother, but there was something he could not endure.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that he did not love his younger brother, but there was something in the matter that he could not endure.

sentences.zh: 是少與我俱，見苦，為生難，故重棄財。

translations.literal: When he was young he was with me. He saw hardship and living was difficult. Therefore, he valued abandoning wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he was young he was with me. He saw the hardship and that living was difficult. Therefore, he valued abandoning wealth.

sentences.zh: 至如少弟者，生而見我富，乘堅驅良逐狡兔，豈知財所從來，故輕棄之，非所惜吝。

translations.literal: As for the young younger brother, born seeing me rich, riding firm and driving good to pursue cunning rabbits. How did he know where wealth came from? Therefore, he lightly abandoned it. It was not what he cherished and was stingy about.
translations.idiomatic: As for the young younger brother, he was born seeing me rich, riding firm carriages and driving good horses to pursue cunning rabbits. How did he know where wealth came from? Therefore, he lightly abandoned it. It was not what he cherished and was stingy about.

sentences.zh: 前日吾所為欲遣少子，固為其能棄財故也。

translations.literal: The other day, when I wished to send the younger son, it was precisely because he can abandon wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The other day, when I wished to send the younger son, it was precisely because he can abandon wealth.

sentences.zh: 而長者不能，故卒以殺其弟，事之理也，無足悲者。

translations.literal: But the elder son could not. Therefore, he in the end caused his younger brother's death. Such is the way of affairs. There is nothing worth grieving over.
translations.idiomatic: But the elder son could not. Therefore, he in the end caused his younger brother's death. Such is the way of affairs. There is nothing worth grieving over.

sentences.zh: 吾日夜固以望其喪之來也。」

translations.literal: I day night certainly expected his funeral come.'
translations.idiomatic: I day and night certainly expected his funeral to come.'

sentences.zh: 故范蠡三徙，成名於天下，非茍去而已，所止必成名。

translations.literal: Therefore, Fan Li in three moves achieved fame in the world. He did not casually depart only. Wherever he stopped he certainly achieved fame.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, Fan Li in three moves achieved fame in the world. He did not casually depart only. Wherever he stopped he certainly achieved fame.

sentences.zh: 卒老死于陶，故世傳曰陶朱公。

translations.literal: He finally aged and died in Tao. Therefore, the world transmitted Tao Zhu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He finally aged and died in Tao. Therefore, the world transmitted the name Tao Zhu Gong.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：禹之功大矣，漸九川，定九州，至于今諸夏艾安。

translations.literal: Grand Historian said: Yu merit great, regulated nine rivers, settled nine provinces, until now various Xia peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian said: Yu's merit was great. He regulated the nine rivers and settled the nine provinces. Until now the various Xia are peaceful.

sentences.zh: 及苗裔句踐，苦身焦思，終滅彊吳，北觀兵中國，以尊周室，號稱霸王。

translations.literal: And his descendant Gou Jian tormented his body with anxious thought, finally extinguished mighty Wu, marched his troops north into the Central States to honor the Zhou royal house, and was styled hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: And his descendant Gou Jian tormented his body with anxious thought, finally extinguished mighty Wu, marched his troops north into the Central States to honor the Zhou royal house, and was styled hegemon.

sentences.zh: 句踐可不謂賢哉！

translations.literal: Gou Jian can not be called worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Can Gou Jian not be called worthy!

sentences.zh: 蓋有禹之遺烈焉。

translations.literal: Indeed he has Yu's remaining illustrious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed he has Yu's remaining illustrious deeds.

sentences.zh: 范蠡三遷皆有榮名，名垂後世。

translations.literal: Fan Li's three moves all had glorious names. Names hung for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li's three moves all had glorious names. His name hung for later generations.

sentences.zh: 臣主若此，欲毋顯得乎！

translations.literal: When minister and lord are like this, how could they fail to achieve renown!
translations.idiomatic: When minister and lord are like this, how could they fail to achieve renown!
